cells.value: Operating Conditions
Typical contributors
Impacts
Start-up; see (4.2.1)

Well bore clean-up:
- higher salinity
- production of solids
- lower pH

- more severe effluent chemistry
- adsorption of inhibitors on solids, increasing inhibitor requirements
- some inhibitors do not work well in high salinity environments
- high salinity environments may require different corrosion resistant alloys
Mill scale conversion to loosen FeS

- adsorption of inhibitors on the mill scale increasing inhibitor requirements
- potential operation problems in downstream units with scale deposits
Spent HCl acids (neutralized); see (4.2.9)

- much higher chlorides (up to 300,000 ppm)
- production of solids
- lower pH

- potential degraded inhibitor performance and FeS scale instability
- adsorption of inhibitors increasing inhibitor requirements
Shut-in and fuel gas blanketed for long time; see (4.2.3 to 4.2.5)
Conversion of FeS to FeCO₃
- no corrosion protection from FeS scales during restart. FeCO₃ scales not as protective as FeS scales
Turn around (line open to moist air); see (4.2.6)
Conversion of FeS into Fe(OH)₃ and re-conversion to greigite on start up.

- no corrosion protection from FeS scales during restart. Greigite not as protective as other types of FeS scales
- potential degraded inhibitor performance
Methanol injection; see (4.2.10)

Methanol condensation behaviour.
O₂ injected with the methanol

- potential degraded inhibitor performance
- chemical reaction creates elemental sulphur which is corrosive
- destroys protective scale
